key_insight: A recurrent forecaster’s usually unused initial state can serve as a conditioning interface, modestly improving forecasts without changing backbone weights.
engineering_relevance: Small state-writing heads offer a lightweight way to inject spectral context or series-associated text into recurrent time-series foundation models.
method: Freeze the xLSTM-based TiRex backbone and train a small head to initialize its recurrent state.
Condition the state on spectral summaries or embeddings of text attached to each series.
Compare against static states, parameter-matched LoRA adapters, and full fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Spectral conditioning reduced mean GiftEval MASE by 0.175% across all tested seeds; on six MoTime datasets, text conditioning added reductions of 0.15–0.41% of baseline MASE on four datasets.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and TiRex-specific, with small gains concentrated in mLSTM blocks and strongest at short context.
paper_title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
